scope: P4 navigation shutdown behavior and live stale-input fault path; no controller, PX4, or flight

behavior: NavigationNode disables rclpy automatic signal shutdown. SIGINT requests goal ABORT while the executor keeps spinning; shutdown waits for active action callbacks and allows one second for the action result service before stopping the executor and destroying node/context.
TaskSupervisor.abort emits ABORTED with clear_trajectory=true; the action execute callback completes the active action as ABORTED and is tracked until its callback exits.
The mapping runtime probe and localization freshness probe explicitly handle SIGINT, drain their executors, and save partial reports before destroying nodes/context.
Action goal rejection logs the exact failed readiness, freshness, epoch, frame, downstream subscription, or goal-validation check without changing accept/reject behavior.
Navigation logs localization receipt age at stale-gate activation, status and optimized-odometry callback gaps after recovery, and timer callback gaps exceeding the freshness guard.

The duplicate user subscription to every /clock message was replaced with rclpy Clock.create_jump_callback using a negative-jump threshold of one nanosecond; the callback preserves clock_regression fail-closed behavior and leaves rclpy TimeSource as the only per-message clock subscriber.

All logger calls formerly inside shared NavigationNode state-lock sections now run after the same state checks, pose/core updates, and task event processing complete and the lock is released. Conditions and message text are preserved; no PX4/control publisher or task-state transition was changed.

Run #29 also logged 3.24–3.32 s status/timer/optimized-odometry callback gaps and asynchronous Destroyable exceptions; these successful shutdown observations do not qualify input stability or clean teardown. The #32 clock-jump build was not live-qualified: #33 planned then hit localization_status_stale before the requested shutdown terminal result, and #35 failed readiness before goal acceptance. Current clock-jump build #32 also passed once in #42 using a probe that sent SIGINT directly to the navigation node PID immediately after matching READY: action result was navigation_node_shutdown ABORT, matching traj_server ABORT, zero READY afterward, and process exit code 0. Run #53 on the same build #32 with a run-private /clock relay also passed once: a fresh TRACKING epoch and nonempty map/depth gate produced a matching B-spline/READY; immediate direct-PID SIGINT returned navigation_node_shutdown ABORT, matching traj_server ABORT, zero READY after ABORT, and navigation exit code 0. The relay was configured for 150 Hz and measured about 102 Hz over this short run; this is diagnostic-only and does not qualify repeatability or a production rate. In #53 the same current build with a run-private clock relay planned and passed the active-goal SIGINT path once. Run #54 separately passed caller cancellation with a matching trajectory ABORT and zero later READY, then verified the navigation process stayed alive until an idle SIGINT and exited 0; this idle shutdown is distinct from active-goal shutdown. Independent canonical-clock run #62 also passed: all tracked external freshness checks held for 1.002 s, matching B-spline/READY was followed by SIGINT, matching action/traj_server ABORT, zero later READY, and exit code 0. Navigation nevertheless logged 3.79–3.82 s callback gaps before action acceptance. #61/#62 provide two path observations, not a stability pass. Canonical-clock run #63 also passed the matching B-spline/READY, action and traj_server ABORT, zero-later-READY path with both exit codes 0, but its observer started after the earlier callback gaps. Runs #64/#65 are excluded: #64 hit the Fast DDS domain 233 port limit before sensors, and #65 kept motion active before localization initialization and remained propagated_stale with no goal. Run #66 repeated the shutdown path after stationary VINS warm-up and observer-first startup; matching action/traj_server ABORT, zero later READY and exit code 0 were observed. This is four effective normal-clock shutdown observations (#61/#62/#63/#66), not a stability or clean-teardown pass; #66 still logged asynchronous Destroyable exceptions. Normal-clock runs #68 and #69 also passed the matching active-goal shutdown path; #69 recorded a 1.878 s _execute_goal_impl lock hold. #71 passed with goal transaction sub-operations under 1.864 ms despite multi-second pre-goal callbacks; #72 passed with a 53 ms maximum lock hold; #73 passed while _on_odometry held the state lock for 4.011 s. Run #70 is excluded for high-volume instrumentation overhead. #74 had no goal after its pre-goal freshness gate timed out; #76 had no goal because localization was telemetry_stale and the map was empty. Run #75 adds one more effective normal-clock active-goal shutdown observation (#61/#62/#63/#66/#68/#69/#71/#72/#73/#75 = ten), but also exposed a 3.518 s logger call inside the state lock. Ten path observations do not establish input stability, clean teardown, trajectory tracking, arrival, or formal P4 acceptance.

shutdown_qualification.navigation_status_delivery: Run #24 aborted localization_status_stale while the independent observer still received status at roughly 50 ms intervals. Run #26 logged a 0.707 s navigation optimized-odometry callback gap while its independent adapted-odometry subscriber had a maximum 154.5 ms gap. Run #27 UST data showed navigation status RMW takes with a maximum 200.104 ms source-time gap (p95 50.727 ms) and optimized-odometry takes with a maximum 143.702 ms gap (p95 133.981 ms), without reproducing a long callback gap. Run #29 logged navigation status/timer/optimized-odometry gaps of 3.258/3.242/3.316 s; independent adapted-odometry receipt gaps peaked at 189.4 ms, while independent status samples had a 1.30 s maximum gap and raw propagated receipt gaps peaked at 66.4 ms. Run #30 reached matching B-spline/READY then aborted pose_stale, with 1.746/1.738/1.795 s navigation status/timer/odometry gaps; its independent adapted-odometry subscriber peaked at 229 ms. Run #30 thread sampling showed the navigation Python process main thread near one CPU core (about 105–115% sampled during the callback gap; 76% average over the sample), but the UST attempt wrote metadata only and no event streams. These observations support intermittent scheduling/processing delay inside the navigation process, but status-source gaps also occurred and no Python stack or repeatable trace locates the cause among the executor, callback work, or RMW delivery. Run #30 independent status history also had a 1.102 s maximum gap, and raw IMU receipt gaps peaked at 448 ms, so the producer/transport path is not fully continuous either. Run #31 Python stacks show a worker executing the duplicate per-message _on_clock callback during 3.9 s navigation gaps, with four 100% main-thread CPU samples; stacks still do not identify one blocking function. After replacing that subscriber, #33 had shorter ~0.5 s gaps and four 58.3% samples but still stale-aborted; independent raw IMU receipt gaps were 420 ms. Post-cleanup #35 had 1.115 s IMU, 400 ms optimized-odometry, and 347 ms propagated-IMU receipt gaps despite source timestamp intervals no larger than 15/99/15 ms. This points to a delivery/scheduling gap somewhere in the live pipeline, but does not identify its source. Current-build run #42 passed direct-PID active-goal SIGINT, but still logged 1.700/1.705/2.090 s status/timer/optimized-odometry gaps and the independent IMU receipt observer peaked at 1.141 s. Four stack samples showed 100% main-thread CPU and no duplicate _on_clock frame; callback workers were in odometry, localization, action-loop and warning-logger code. This confirms the clock subscriber was removed but does not establish why CPU or delivery gaps remain. In #62 the external status/odom/map/depth/pair gate had zero failed checks over its 1.002 s stable interval, while navigation itself logged 3.792 s status and odometry gaps and a 3.816 s timer gap before accepting the action. The observations are from the same run but are not aligned with a high-resolution common timeline; they cannot distinguish node-local processing/delivery from source or transport gaps. In #63 the independent timeline began after navigation logged its multi-second callback gaps, so it could not align them. Run #66 corrected the order: during the navigation 0.419 s optimized-odometry callback gap, the independent observer received 3 optimized-odometry samples (bounded maximum receipt gap 115.868 ms), 9 valid TRACKING status samples (maximum 50.936 ms), and 2 pose/depth pairs (bounded maximum 231.708 ms). This same-window contrast supports a navigation-node receive/scheduling-path investigation, but cannot distinguish RMW reader delivery from executor selection or callback scheduling. #65 is excluded because motion started before stationary VINS initialization and localization remained propagated_stale. Runs #67–#73 aligned executor and callback traces to an independent timeline. #67 passed the observer freshness gate but navigation selected only five status and four odometry callbacks and rejected the goal as not ready; this is a local visibility symptom, not proof of a DDS root cause. #68 had an independent odometry gap of 889 ms. #69 measured a 1.878 s lock hold in _execute_goal_impl. #71 measured up to 2.976 s callback duration before goal dispatch while goal transaction operations remained below 1.864 ms. #72 reproduced only a 53 ms lock hold. #73 measured a 4.011 s _on_odometry lock hold while independent status and odometry receipts in that exact interval continued at maximum gaps 53.478/117.797 ms. Run #75 instrumented the warning boundary: get_logger().warning lasted 3.518167 s, the containing state lock held 3.518342 s, and a localization callback waited 3.518046 s; same-window observer status/odometry maximum gaps were 52.417/112.796 ms. This directly attributes that observed lock stall to synchronous warning logging, but does not explain why the logger/output path blocked. The targeted change first moved the odometry warning after lock release; the final source also moves the other shared-lock logger calls after their state/event updates. Synthetic regressions block both the warning and accepted-goal INFO and verify the lock remains available. #76 did not reach TRACKING/map readiness and predates the final expanded change, so live fix qualification is pending.

All external gate checks were fresh for 1.002 s, but navigation logged 3.79–3.82 s callback gaps and two asynchronous Destroyable exceptions; EGO logged input/planner errors. Exit code 0 does not establish clean teardown, stable input delivery, or formal P4 acceptance.

normal_clock_active_goal_shutdown_run_63.ego_input_loss_timing: All 36 odom/depth lost lines occurred after trajectory ABORT.
normal_clock_active_goal_shutdown_run_63.qualification: Shutdown path repeat only. Observer began after the earlier callback gaps, so no alignment claim; post-ABORT EGO input warnings do not qualify planning instability.

normal_clock_active_goal_precondition_do.failure: Fast DDS calculated port number too high; D435i depth topic did not appear.
normal_clock_active_goal_precondition_do.qualification: Excluded precondition failure; no action goal or shutdown attempt.

observer_first_startup_confounded_run_65.result: FAIL_PRECONDITION_PROPAGATED_STALE; no active goal or shutdown path.
observer_first_startup_confounded_run_65.qualification: Excluded: motion began before stationary VINS initialization, observer, and navigation; this startup order confounds the comparison.

normal_clock_active_goal_aligned_observe.result: PASS_ACTIVE_GOAL_SHUTDOWN_ABORT; canonical /clock; independent observer timeline covered navigation startup and callback gap.
normal_clock_active_goal_aligned_observe.control_boundary: One d435i_bridge /clock publisher, /clock_raw absent; no controller/PX4/control node observed; PX4 control-topic audit empty.
normal_clock_active_goal_aligned_observe.qualification: One active shutdown observation with same-window independent receipts. Evidence narrows the next diagnostic to navigation-node executor/RMW delivery; it does not isolate the cause. Solver errors preceded the successful plan; two Destroyable exceptions remain.

normal_clock_nav_local_status_visibility.details: External 1.0 s freshness gate passed with zero failures, but NavigationNode rejected the goal. During the probe window its executor selected only 5 status and 4 odometry callbacks while the observer received 30 status and 15 optimized odometry samples; this is a reader/executor visibility symptom, not an isolated root cause.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_run_68.details: Freshness gates passed; matching B-spline/READY, navigation_node_shutdown action ABORT, matching traj_server ABORT, zero later READY and process exit 0. Callback delivery still showed long tails; independent optimized-odometry receipt had an 888.670 ms maximum gap, so this run does not isolate a navigation-only gap.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_lock_outlie.details: Matching active-goal shutdown path passed. Run-private lock trace measured _execute_goal_impl holding the node state lock for 1.878 s, with input/timer workers waiting about 1.88–1.90 s; this single outlier does not identify a consistent cause.

normal_clock_high_volume_instrumentation.details: No goal. The high-volume 3.84 MB/18,260-event diagnostic trace coincided with freshness-gate failures and multi-second lock waits; excluded from root-cause inference.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_fast_goal_t.details: Matching active-goal shutdown path passed. Goal validation, core submit, EGO publish, and accept logging each took at most 1.864 ms; before goal dispatch, several navigation callbacks had about 2.97 s duration while the independent status/odometry observer remained comparatively fresh. The goal transaction was not a consistently slow operation.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_short_lock_.details: Matching active-goal shutdown path passed. Sparse lock trace showed a maximum 53.394 ms hold; independent status/odometry maximum receipt gaps were 52.223/116.332 ms. No multi-second lock stall reproduced.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_odom_lock_s.details: Matching active-goal shutdown path passed. _on_odometry held the navigation state lock for 4.011 s; localization/odometry callback workers waited about 4.027–4.031 s. In the same lock interval the independent observer received status every at most 53.478 ms and optimized odometry every at most 117.797 ms. This establishes a node-local lock stall but not its internal cause.

normal_clock_pre_goal_input_failure_run_.details: The probe did not observe fresh localization, map, depth and pose/depth inputs stable for 1 s within 30 s; no goal was dispatched. No executor trace was created because the run-private package copy omitted package glue and was not imported. Excluded from navigation callback and logger diagnosis.

normal_clock_active_shutdown_logger_lock.details: Matching active-goal shutdown path passed. A run-private timestamp around the conditional optimized-odometry warning measured one logger call at 3.518167 s; the enclosing state-lock hold was 3.518342 s and a localization callback waited 3.518046 s. In that same interval, the independent status and odometry receipt maximum gaps were 52.417/112.796 ms. Three further warning calls took 200.313, 37.389 and 67.193 ms. This directly attributes the observed long lock hold to synchronous warning logging in this diagnostic run; it does not explain why the logger/output path blocked.

post_fix_pre_goal_telemetry_stale_run_76.details: After the logger-outside-lock change was built, the live probe reported localization telemetry_stale and an empty map before any goal; no active-goal behavior or live fix verification occurred. Excluded from runtime-fix qualification.

stale_instrumented_active_goal_run_83_ex.qualification: Functional route only; excluded from logger-fix qualification because the run-private instrumented module was stale and held the accepted-goal INFO call under the lock.

current_source_active_goal_shutdown_run_.localization: 33 valid TRACKING status samples; 1,414 map points; all one-second pre-goal checks passed.
current_source_active_goal_shutdown_run_.trajectory: One matching B-spline, two PositionCommand samples including READY and matching ABORT; action result navigation_node_shutdown ABORT; no READY after abort.
current_source_active_goal_shutdown_run_.lock_diagnostics: Zero state_lock_slow events above 5 ms; no warning was triggered in this short run.

guard_from_source.behavior: Health.freshness reports propagated_stale if either raw VINS imu_propagate source age or receipt age converted to ROS-clock seconds exceeds its configured guard; once TRACKING, the failure locks the session.

propagated_freshness_diagnostic.runs_10_and_11: No propagated_stale status was observed in either 20-second read-only freshness window. Probe-side raw source age was at most 6 ms. Wall receipt interval maxima were 63.085 ms and 84.628 ms at observed clock rates 0.5737 and 0.5722; these subscriber measurements do not prove the adapter received samples at the same instants.
propagated_freshness_diagnostic.qualification: Run #08 propagated-stale failure remains unexplained and the 0.4 s EGO mapping timeout remains PROVISIONAL.

runs_81_82_and_current_policy_review.finding: Run #81 observed propagated source age 63 ms against the then-50 ms guard while receipt-age estimate was 59 ms; policy now uses a PROVISIONAL 120 ms propagated source-age limit. Run #82 then locked on imu_stale when a separate 362 ms wall receipt gap exceeded the unchanged 200 ms simulated receipt guard. No further widening was made.

navigation_diagnostic_tests.environment: Jazzy final navigation overlay #77; ROS_DOMAIN_ID=228; synthetic ROS peers; no simulator, controller or PX4.
navigation_diagnostic_tests.result: PASS: 10 task-state tests. ROS action adapter passes action routing, caller cancel, stale-epoch rejection, clock-regression abort, frozen-clock stale detection and active-goal shutdown; intentionally blocked odometry warning and accepted-goal INFO each leave the shared state lock available.

steady_time_navigation_build_and_tests_r.result: PASS: isolated Jazzy uav_navigation build; 10 task-state tests and ROS action adapter integration passed, including a frozen-/clock stale-guard case with use_sim_time=true.

clock_jump_callback_build_and_tests_run_.result: PASS: isolated Jazzy build of uav_navigation; one package finished. The corrected synthetic tests then passed 10 task-state cases and ROS action integration, including a 1 ns clock rollback, frozen-/clock steady-time freshness guard, and active-goal shutdown ABORT.

odometry_warning_outside_lock_build_and_.result: PASS: isolated Jazzy build of uav_navigation in a fresh build/install directory; 10 task-state tests and ROS action adapter regression tests pass.

shared_state_lock_logging_build_and_test.result: PASS: isolated fresh Jazzy build/install of uav_navigation (1/1); 10 task-state tests; ROS action integration including both blocked-logger concurrency regressions.

clock_jump_callback_diagnostic.change: Replace the navigation node’s duplicate per-message /clock subscription with rclpy Clock.create_jump_callback at a -1 ns threshold. Use TimeJump.delta to reconstruct the previous clock value, seed the core clock state, and call update_clock so an actual regression still aborts the active goal and clears the keyed trajectory.
clock_jump_callback_diagnostic.why: Run #31 stack snapshots captured the navigation worker in _on_clock alongside timer, odometry and warning-logger callbacks; the main thread measured 100% CPU during four 120 ms samples. This identified a concrete, low-risk load candidate, not a proven single root cause.
clock_jump_callback_diagnostic.build_and_synthetic_result: Run #32 isolated Jazzy build passed. Ten task-state tests and adapter action integration passed, including a one-nanosecond rollback producing clock_regression ABORT/cancel, forward-time recovery, frozen-/clock watchdog behavior, and active shutdown ABORT.

clock_jump_run_33.interpretation: The >3.8 s callback gap from #31 did not recur in this sample and no per-message _on_clock frame appeared in the sampled stacks, but the goal became stale before shutdown. One run does not prove the code change caused the lower sampled CPU or shorter gap.

run_34_environment_exclusion.reason: The 64 MiB container /dev/shm was full; the localization observer and Gazebo sensor launch exited with Bus error before /sensors/d435i/depth appeared. Twenty-two ROS CLI daemon caches and 410 unreferenced Fast DDS shared-memory entries were cleared after confirming no live ROS node or mapping used them; #35 was run after cleanup.

post_cleanup_run_35.ego_input_loss: At sim time 4.819 s, last occupancy update was 4.386 s; EGO logged odometry/depth loss with its 0.4 s timeout and 15 synchronized depth/pose samples.

base_image_attempt_36.result: EXCLUDED: run used the base image rather than d435i-vins:dev, so VINS could not load libceres.so.4. No navigation goal was attempted; this was a test setup error, not evidence against the derived image.

setsid_group_check_run_37.result: EXCLUDED_FROM_SHUTDOWN: matching B-spline/READY was reached, but wrapper falsely treated the setsid child as exited by testing a nonexistent process group and never sent SIGINT. Probe timed out with no action result.

freshness_precondition_run_38.result: No active goal: fresh TRACKING odometry and a nonempty map were not observed; localization reported a 3.475 s callback gap and propagated_stale.

invalid_domain_run_39.result: Excluded: ROS_DOMAIN_ID=233 exceeds Fast DDS port range; D435i topic precondition failed before navigation.

pose_stale_race_run_40.result: Matching B-spline/READY reached; pose_stale ABORT occurred about 98 ms after READY, before the wrapper’s 250 ms polling loop delivered SIGINT. Not a shutdown pass.

incomplete_harness_edit_run_41.result: Excluded: wrapper patch assertion failed before the live probe; temporary container removed before navigation started.

current_build_active_shutdown_run_42.teardown: Two asynchronous Destroyable exceptions appeared after the supervisor log ended; clean teardown is not established.

live_comparison.interpretation: The duplicate per-message /clock subscriber is absent from later stack samples. Run #33 showed shorter gaps/lower sampled CPU, but current-build #42 again sampled 100% main-thread CPU with 1.7–2.1 s callback gaps and a 1.141 s independent IMU receipt gap. The change preserves clock-regression semantics and may reduce one callback source, but it did not resolve live scheduling/freshness instability; no single root cause is established. The no-goal #44 timeline showed receipt tails in D435i IMU and EGO outputs under high-rate observation, so it is diagnostic only. Reduced-observer #45 still measured 49–82% main-thread CPU in four short windows, with all captured Python stacks in rclpy executor wait-set code and callback workers idle; this does not isolate a cause or justify a production change.

run_43_wrapper_startup_exclusion.reason: Wrapper enabled nounset before sourcing /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash and stopped on unset AMENT_TRACE_SETUP_FILES before launching any probe or project process.

run_44_no_goal_timing_diagnostic.no_goal_or_control: No action goal client, PX4 bridge, controller, or control output.
run_44_no_goal_timing_diagnostic.interpretation: Source and receipt timing diverge in some streams, including a 1.186 s IMU receipt interval despite a 5 ms maximum source interval. EGO pose receipt gaps reach 2.381 s while paired output source intervals reach 132 ms. High-rate observers add material CPU load, so this does not isolate publisher, DDS, or executor delay.

run_45_no_goal_navigation_cpu_stack_diag.no_goal_or_control: No action goal client, PX4 bridge, controller, or control output.
run_45_no_goal_navigation_cpu_stack_diag.worker_threads: Four executor workers were in concurrent.futures.thread._worker at all captured dumps.
run_45_no_goal_navigation_cpu_stack_diag.shutdown_warning: The only navigation stale warning was emitted during teardown (status receipt age 0.537 s; optimized odometry receipt age 0.642 s); not counted as an in-run failure.
run_45_no_goal_navigation_cpu_stack_diag.cleanup: Wrapper and stack sampler exited 0. Container inspection found no project process; /dev/shm used 2 MiB of 512 MiB.
run_45_no_goal_navigation_cpu_stack_diag.interpretation: High main-thread CPU persisted without the #44 high-rate observers, but the four stack samples only place execution in normal executor wait-set code. A single sampled path cannot distinguish repeated ready-entity processing, RMW activity, graph work, or another native wait-set cost.

clock_jump_callback_diagnostic.qualification: The replacement preserves clock-regression semantics in synthetic integration, and current build #32 passed one active-goal live SIGINT shutdown in #42. Runs #44 and #45 extend no-goal timing and CPU diagnostics but do not qualify freshness, executor stability, or clean repeated teardown. The cause remains unresolved. No freshness guard was relaxed.
clock_jump_callback_diagnostic.next_diagnostic_step: Profile a current-build no-goal run with low-overhead executor wakeup/callback counts and RMW/native CPU samples aligned to sensor source and receipt timestamps. Keep guards and timeout unchanged; only repeat active-goal cancel/shutdown after the delivery and scheduler behavior are understood.

no_goal_executor_diagnostics.scope: No-goal, no-controller, no-PX4 diagnostic runs; no production source or config changed.

run_46_excluded.reason: Run-private executor hook re-raised inner generator StopIteration, causing the navigation node to exit with RuntimeError. The wrapper failed to detect the child failure and wrote a completion marker; exclude this run.

run_47_excluded.reason: The instrumented generator forced a counter flush on every normal StopIteration, producing 11,741 records / 2.9 MB and perturbing the run. The wrapper was interrupted before the planned observation window completed.

run_48_type_only.observation: About 355–414 ready callbacks per two-second window; entity types only, no topic attribution. Consistent with #45 short CPU samples but does not identify the cause.

run_49_topic_resolved.observation: Navigation remained alive; correlation between /clock readiness and executor CPU is not a root-cause proof.

run_55_normal_clock_matched_observers.clock_relay: Disabled; canonical d435i_bridge was the sole /clock publisher.
run_55_normal_clock_matched_observers.teardown: Navigation stale warning appeared only after upstream teardown; all observer status samples during the window were valid; project processes absent after wrapper cleanup.
run_55_normal_clock_matched_observers.interpretation: Against matched #52 observers, #55 had /clock readiness near #49 and median generator CPU 0.644 s/s versus #52 0.373 s/s, while both status observers saw valid samples. This supports association with ready /clock rate but does not identify the callback/RMW/native cost or establish sole causality.

stack_sampling.interpretation: 80 instantaneous snapshots localize frequent frames but are not CPU-weighted and do not establish a root cause.

run_57_high_rate_stack_samples.interpretation: WaitSet and waitable methods are frequent instantaneous stack positions, not measured CPU shares. No root cause identified; diagnostic only.

clock_relay_diagnostics.scope: Run-private sensor bridge mapping /clock to /clock_raw plus a wall-time relay to /clock. Canonical project configuration and source were unchanged; no action goal, controller, PX4, or control output in #50–#52.

run_50_50hz.localization: Invalid/future IMU status and no optimized-odometry readiness in steady windows; CPU reduction is confounded. Relay teardown logged shutdown exceptions.

run_52_150hz_no_goal.comparison: About 45% below #49 median executor generator CPU ratio (0.676 s/s); all 825/825 low-rate status samples were TRACKING/fresh_inputs_and_usable_solver. Single diagnostic only; does not establish a production clock-rate setting or sole cause. One stale warning appeared after upstream teardown.

run_53_active_goal.control_boundary: No controller/PX4 node or /fmu topic; /position_cmd had one publisher (traj_server) and no subscriber.
run_53_active_goal.qualification: Single live planning/shutdown observation; no tracking or arrival.

run_54_caller_cancel_and_idle_shutdown.qualification: One short live observation under run-private relay, no controller or PX4.

run_55_normal_clock_controlled_observer_.comparison: Matched #52 status, executor and stack observers: normal-clock #55 CPU ratio0.644 s/s vs throttled #52 0.373 s/s; status remained valid in both windows. #55 also logged EGO odom/depth timeouts. Correlation only; source/callback cost is unresolved.

logger_lock_diagnostic.interpretation: Synchronous get_logger().warning call dominates the measured _on_odometry lock hold in this one diagnostic run. Cause of the logger call delay is unresolved.
logger_lock_diagnostic.fix: Move every NavigationNode logger call that previously ran within a shared state-lock section until after state/task event processing and lock release; retain the same checks and messages.
logger_lock_diagnostic.synthetic_regression: PASS: separately block the odometry warning and accepted-goal INFO logger calls; in both cases another thread acquires the navigation state lock.
logger_lock_diagnostic.live_fix_status: not_qualified; #76 failed pre-goal under the initial targeted odometry-warning patch; the final expanded shared-lock logging change is build/synthetic-tested only.
